faqs.question: What are some easy Diwali decoration ideas for home?
faqs.answer: Start at the entrance: a marigold-and-mango-leaf toran over the door and five or seven clay diyas on a metal tray at the threshold, about 30–45 minutes and roughly ₹250–600 (October 2026 estimate). Floating wax diyas and marigold heads in a bowl of water take about 20 minutes and keep the flame over water.

faqs.question: How early should I decorate for Diwali 2027?
faqs.answer: Aim to finish by Dhanteras on Wednesday 27 October 2027, since lamps are lit each evening from then through Bhai Dooj on Sunday 31 October. Lakshmi Puja, the main night, is Friday 29 October 2027.

faqs.question: How can I decorate my office desk for Diwali without breaking fire rules?
faqs.answer: Go flameless: three or four battery LED tealights on a small tray and a short paper toran on the desk partition, with nothing plugged in. It takes 15–20 minutes and roughly ₹150–350 per desk (October 2026 estimate); check your facilities team's rules before bringing any plug-in lights.

faqs.question: Should children light diyas at school for Diwali?
faqs.answer: No open flame is the safer rule for a room full of children: they can paint clay diyas and display them unlit, plus chart-paper lanterns on the soft board, with battery tealights only the teacher switches on. Budget about ₹15–30 per child for a diya and paint (October 2026 estimate) and one 40-minute period to make them.

faqs.question: Do Diwali fairy lights need BIS marking?
faqs.answer: Yes. Festival string lights are lighting chains under IS 10322 (Part 5/Sec 7), and MeitY's 2021 compulsory registration order requires them to be registered with BIS. The standard also requires the rated voltage and wattage to be marked on the chain.

faqs.question: How many fairy light strings can I plug into one socket?
faqs.answer: One. Delhi Fire Service advises one appliance per socket and recommends miniature and earth-leakage circuit breakers on the circuit. Stacking extension boards to run several strings is the overloading its advisory warns against.

faqs.question: Can I throw water on a fire from Diwali lights?
faqs.answer: No. Switch off the power supply first, then use dry sand, CO2 or dry powder, as Delhi Fire Service advises; the Uttar Pradesh Fire Services advisory warns against water extinguishers on energised electrical equipment. Keep the two buckets of water for diya and cloth fires.

faqs.question: Is it safe to leave diyas burning overnight?
faqs.answer: The safer habit is to put out or count every flame before bed. The Uttar Pradesh Fire Services advisory asks households to clear curtains, paper, synthetic cloth, oil and ghee from around the puja place after Lakshmi Puja and before going to sleep.

faqs.question: What should I do if someone gets burnt by a diya?
faqs.answer: Cool the burn under running water until the pain eases; the Uttar Pradesh Fire Services advisory says about 10 minutes of cold water. Tamil Nadu Fire and Rescue Services say never to put cream, ointment or oil on it, and a serious burn needs a hospital; the fire control number is 101.

faqs.question: How do I decorate a small balcony for Diwali?
faqs.answer: One warm-white LED string along the railing and clay diyas on the inner ledge, not the outer edge, plugged into a single wall socket. Allow 1–2 hours and roughly ₹200–700 for a 10–12 metre string and two dozen diyas (October 2026 estimate).

faqs.question: Can I send a decorated Diwali to someone in another city?
faqs.answer: Your lights cannot travel, but a greeting can. SubhSandesh's Diwali card lets the recipient light a diya at their door, colour a rangoli until your initials glow and release sky lanterns holding up to six of your photos; it takes about five minutes to make and opens as a private link in any browser. It is a one-person greeting, not decoration.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Diwali Decoration Ideas for Home, Balcony, Office and Classroom

The Diwali decoration ideas that get finished are chosen by space, not by mood board: a toran and diya line at the entrance, a lit puja corner, one string of lights on the balcony, a desk-sized setup at the office and a flameless display in a school classroom. Each idea below carries a setup time and a dated cost estimate, and most take under two hours.

Those times matter because festival preparation runs late. In SubhSandesh's nearest festival data, Raksha Bandhan 2026 (n = 89 pages, not Diwali), 49.4% of pages were built on the festival day itself and 86.1% of the on-time ones within 24 hours of it.

So ideas are sorted by time needed, followed by fire and electrical safety from the Bureau of Indian Standards and three state fire services. Diwali 2027 is Friday 29 October; Dhanteras is Wednesday 27 October.

## What counts as Diwali decoration, and when should it go up in 2027?

Diwali decoration is the lighting, flowers and threshold markings a household puts up to welcome Lakshmi on the new-moon night, led by rows of oil lamps (diyas). Deepavali means a row of lamps, so light, not ornament, is the core of the job.

Most homes clean first and decorate by Dhanteras, so the practical deadline in 2027 is Wednesday 27 October, with lamps lit each evening through Bhai Dooj on Sunday 31 October. Five nights of lights is why the flame and wiring rules below matter more than any colour scheme. Rangoli patterns have their own guide on this blog, so they are left out here.

## Diwali decoration ideas for home, space by space

Each idea gives what it is, who it suits, cost and time. Costs are rough October 2026 market ranges, labelled EST, and vary by city.

### 1. Entrance: a toran and a tray of threshold diyas

Hang a marigold-and-mango-leaf toran over the door and set five or seven clay diyas on a metal tray at the threshold, not on the floor. A tray keeps oil off the tiles and moves every flame at once.

**Suits:** every home, including a one-room flat. **Cost:** about ₹250–600 for fresh flowers, leaves and a dozen diyas (Oct 2026, EST). **Time:** 30–45 minutes.

### 2. Puja corner: a lit backdrop behind the chowki

Drape a cotton saree or dupatta behind the chowki with one LED string behind it so the glow comes through. Keep real diyas in front on a brass plate, an arm's length from the cloth.

**Suits:** homes doing Lakshmi Puja at home on 29 October 2027. **Cost:** about ₹150–400 for an LED string and a plate, using fabric you already own (Oct 2026, EST). **Time:** 45–60 minutes.

### 3. Living room: floating diyas in an urli

Float marigold heads and three or four wax diyas in a wide bowl of water on a low table, away from curtains. Water under the flame is a built-in safety margin.

**Suits:** families with guests visiting through the five days. **Cost:** about ₹300–900 depending on whether you buy an urli (Oct 2026, EST). **Time:** 20 minutes.

### 4. Balcony or terrace: one string of lights and clay lamps on the ledge

Run one warm-white LED string along the railing and line the inner ledge, not the outer edge, with clay diyas. One string in a wall socket is enough; three stacked extension boards is what fire services warn about.

**Suits:** flats where the balcony is the only part visible from the street. **Cost:** about ₹200–700 for one 10–12 metre LED string and two dozen diyas (Oct 2026, EST). **Time:** 1–2 hours.

## Diwali decoration ideas for office

An office desk is a shared, wired space with a fire policy you did not write, so the useful rule is flameless by default. The setup below takes 15–20 minutes, and nothing on it needs a socket.

### 5. Office desk: a battery tealight tray and a paper toran

Put three or four battery LED tealights on a small brass tray, add a short paper toran along your desk partition, and leave the plug points alone. For a team bay, one plugged-in string owned by one person and switched off every evening beats six people bringing one each.

**Suits:** open-plan offices and anyone with a desk near shared wiring. **Cost:** about ₹150–350 per desk (Oct 2026, EST). **Time:** 15–20 minutes.

## Diwali decoration ideas for school classroom

Build a classroom display for children who touch everything: no open flame, nothing plugged in at child height. The case is not abstract: a 2024 study of 191 children admitted with burns at Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College, Aligarh found that [flame burns made up 18% and electrical injuries 14% of cases](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13271701), with 52 of the 191 (27%) admitted from October to December, the festival months.

### 6. Classroom: painted unlit diyas and paper lanterns on the soft board

Give each child one clay diya to paint, display them unlit on a shelf, and hang chart-paper lanterns along the soft board. If the room needs light, the teacher switches on battery tealights.

**Suits:** pre-primary to Class 5, and any room where an adult cannot watch every flame. **Cost:** about ₹15–30 per child for a diya and paint, plus ₹100–200 of chart paper (Oct 2026, EST). **Time:** one 40-minute period to make, 20 minutes to put up.

Tamil Nadu Fire and Rescue Services' [fire safety guide for school students](https://www.tnfrs.tn.gov.in/sub_page_content.php?menu_id=NDM4&submenu_id=ODIy&dept_id=443&lang=MQ==) tells students not to touch electrical equipment without permission or play with fire-related objects. This display needs neither.

## Time and cost by space, compared

The table compares the ideas on setup and safety. Costs are October 2026 estimates, not quotes.

| Space | Setup time | Cost (EST ₹, Oct 2026) | Open flame? | Main safety step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Entrance | 30–45 min | ₹250–600 | Yes, diyas | Diyas on a metal tray, clear of the door curtain |
| Puja corner | 45–60 min | ₹150–400 | Yes, in front of fabric | Clear cloth, oil and ghee before bed |
| Balcony | 1–2 hours | ₹200–700 | Yes, on the inner ledge | One string per socket |
| Office desk | 15–20 min | ₹150–350 | No | Battery lights only |
| Classroom | 40 + 20 min | ₹15–30 per child | No | Unlit diyas, no plug at child height |

The two flameless setups are also the two quickest, so the safe choice and the last-minute choice are the same one. If you have one evening before Dhanteras, do the entrance and the office desk; leave the balcony for a weekend.

## Fire and electrical safety for diyas and fairy lights

Wiring deserves as much care as the flames. Delhi Fire Service says [about 60% of fires are of electric origin](https://dfs.delhi.gov.in/dfs/fire-safety-precautions-against-electricity-0), from short circuits, overheating, overloading and non-standard appliances.

Start with the lights themselves. BIS covers festival string lights under [IS 10322 (Part 5/Sec 7), lighting chains](https://services.bis.gov.in/tmp/tbl5_2024-11-11-04-57_113.pdf), and MeitY's compulsory registration order of 2021 requires them to be registered with BIS. The standard says a chain must be marked with its rated voltage and wattage, must not electrify tinsel or metal decorations, and must have its controller enclosed in non-flammable insulating material.

- **Check the box:** buy a string marked with BIS registration, rated voltage and wattage.
- **One socket, one plug:** Delhi Fire Service advises one appliance per socket, with miniature and earth-leakage circuit breakers.
- **No wires under mats:** wires under carpets, mats or doorways get crushed and short-circuit.
- **Switch off on the way out:** unplug the lights before leaving home or sleeping.

For flames, the [Uttar Pradesh Fire Services advisory](https://uppolice.gov.in/article/en/fire-services) asks households to light diyas only at safe places, to clear curtains, paper, synthetic cloth, oil and ghee from around the puja place after Lakshmi Puja and before bed, and to keep two buckets of water ready. It adds that the fire control number is 101.

The buckets are for diyas, not for a sparking extension board. The same Uttar Pradesh page warns against using water extinguishers on energised electrical equipment, and Delhi Fire Service says to switch off the supply first, then use dry sand, CO2 or dry powder. For a burn, Tamil Nadu Fire and Rescue Services' [Diwali safety tips](https://www.tnfrs.tn.gov.in/sub_page_content.php?menu_id=NDM4&submenu_id=Nzg2&dept_id=443&lang=MQ==) say to wear cotton and never to put cream, ointment or oil on the burnt area.

## Decorating for someone who will not be home

Some people you would decorate for will spend 29 October 2027 in another city, where your lit balcony does nothing for them. SubhSandesh's Diwali card answers that case only: it is a one-person greeting, not a decoration tool.

The recipient finds a diya at their door with a tag from you, lights a row of wish diyas, colours a rangoli until your initials glow, and lets go of sky lanterns holding up to six of your photos. It takes about five minutes to make and opens as a private link in any browser, which matters because 48.3% of SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone (measured 24 September 2026). If that sounds right, you can [make an interactive Diwali card with sky lanterns and your photos](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali).

For a partner in another city rather than a parent, an ["I miss you" page with a reunion countdown](https://subhsandesh.in/missyou-gf) fits better, though it is not a Diwali design. It carries the distance itself, which is the real subject when the lights are in one city and the person is in another.

## When these decoration ideas are the wrong choice

Flame-based ideas are wrong in three places: a home with a toddler who walks, a hostel or rented room whose rules ban open flame, and any office where facilities has said no. Use flameless versions of ideas 1–4 there.

In a housing society, check the rules on exterior lights and drilling before buying anything that needs a hook. Some families keep the first Diwali after a death quiet, so ask before decorating someone else's home. And SubhSandesh loses outright for anyone in the same house on 29 October, where a real diya you lit together beats any link.

All ₹ costs and setup times are labelled October 2026 estimates (EST). The only price data seen was on a ranking retailer (a competitor for this keyword), so no price source is cited.

The BIS lighting-chains note sits at a services.bis.gov.in/tmp/ path and may move; it prints no publication date, so none is recorded. Commercial consultant pages cite the standard as Part 5 Section 9; the BIS document says Section 7, which the post follows.
